correctness.rationale: An independent model argument starts with the union of star simplices, which intersect only in singleton vertices. In each star, retract equivariantly onto the tree of segments from its barycenter to its vertices: for a unique largest coordinate, the point maps to its arm at parameter largest minus second-largest; ties map to the center. This fixes the tree and star intersections; the straight-line homotopy is equivariant. All other faces are the exceptional triangles on the three ground edges of a ground triangle. Each of their boundary edges maps homeomorphically to the two arms through the common star center; the quotient homotopy pushout (use invariant collars on the triangle boundaries) therefore gives the edge-midpoint-subdivided ground two-skeleton model after taking cyclic orbits. This verifies the reduction independently of the cited stronger PL model. The skeleton is simply connected. A nonidentity element of order d fixes a point only on a support that is a union of label-orbits of size d, with constant coordinates on each orbit. As support has size at most three, exactly orders two and three have fixed points, in numbers n/2 and n/3. The source's blanket pointwise iff about invariant supports needs the coordinate condition, which is used in its ensuing midpoint/barycenter calculation. Armstrong gives the stated quotient by the subgroup generated by these elements. Burnside on barycentric cells gives chi=1+r_n; the quotient model is a two-dimensional CW complex, so H2 is free, higher homology vanishes, and the finite pi1 determines H1 and forces rank H1=0. For n=6 the quotient model is simply connected of H2 rank two; Hurewicz and homological Whitehead give the wedge. The two-dimensional statements concern a model, not the dimension of the original geometric quotient. The uploaded verifier was inspected, not executed; its Smith forms would check only homology of finite instances, not general pi1 or the equivariant reduction.

originality.rationale: Existing exact and stronger results together give the full claimed conclusion by direct standard applications, not just a similar result at the same parameters. The free widths and the rank at ALL widths were already stated. At singular widths the earlier equivariant model gives a simply connected two-dimensional source and a two-dimensional quotient model, and the earlier general fixed-locus theorem gives exactly the fixed elements. With these known inputs, Armstrong gives C_{n/gcd(n,6)} at once, H1 is its abelianization and H2 is free of the already known rank. At six this makes the two-dimensional model simply connected with rank-two H2, so its sphere wedge is the standard Hurewicz–Whitehead consequence. No novel intermediate mathematical step is needed. This is a finding of direct prior implication, not a claim that one earlier paper explicitly printed the entire statement.
